saw_lines: Romance ebook readers buy the next book in a series they like, and decide from the first line of the blurb.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line of your ad, before any price or proof is seen.
Your 5 of 13 copy ads reuse one exact copy, so the same message repeats across the account. Keep that copy but swap the opening line and creative in each.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 12 Oct 2026
points: 5 of your 13 copy ads run one exact copy, so a reader who sees two sees the same story twice. Keep that copy, change the opening line and creative in each of those 5 ads, and test two new openers.
0 of 13 copy ads carry a proof number, so a buyer weighing a new ebook has no reason to trust the story yet. Pull one real number, such as a review count, and lead every ad with it.

5 of your 13 copy ads open on the same opener, “vijf warme, romantische feelgoodverhalen vol”, while the other 8 each open differently. Test two new angles against it, a price line and a first chapter hook.
Your median ad runs 185 words and the longest 414, so the reason to buy sits far below where readers stop. Keep each ad to two lines, a price or first chapter hook, then the buy button.
